mission: Desh warns Ben explicitly: the group is fracturing. His operational concern reveals he cares about more than logistics — he's invested in these people and their mission.
why_now: Desh's arc: moment_of_truth — his concern goes beyond professional obligation to genuine investment
conflict: Desh delivers the assessment Ben needs but doesn't want: Torin is separating. Sera is rigid. Kael is watching for the exit. The group will not survive another crisis as currently configured.
turning_point: Desh: 'I didn't come here to watch another good person convince themselves they're the only answer.' He means Jacen. He means Torin. He means Ben, if Ben doesn't change course.
opening_hook: Desh doesn't frame it as a warning. He frames it as a debrief. 'Let me walk you through the team status.' It's the most frightening sentence Ben has heard on this trip.
closing_hook: Desh's final assessment: 'You need to give them a reason to stay that isn't you telling them to.' Ben doesn't have that reason yet. But he knows where to look — somewhere in the Codex notes he bookmarked and hasn't revisited.
emotional_trajectory: Professional assessment -> personal investment revealed -> the challenge to Ben's leadership approach

stakes.personal: Desh's arc transition — from obligation to chosen commitment
stakes.interpersonal: The group's survival as a functioning unit
stakes.external: A fractured group cannot face Veraine at Veranthos

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — cockpit, night cycle
sensory_details: Instrument lights; Desh's voice — steady, professional, and for the first time openly emotional; the nav display showing Veranthos's system approaching; countdown timer Desh posted on the bulkhead
action_beats: Desh pulls out his datapad and walks Ben through each team member's status — clinical, precise, devastating
Desh taps the countdown timer he posted on the bulkhead without looking at it
Ben stares at the Codex file bookmark on his datapad after Desh leaves — the resonance note waiting
notes: Desh's arc: moment_of_truth — his operational concern revealing genuine care. The Jacen reference is powerful because Desh is the only person who was there with Ben, watching it happen in real time.
